description: Somos unos chicos amantes de la campana de Gauss.
summary: Cropy is a mobile-first web app, a decision-support tool that helps farmers in extreme climates decide what to plant, when to plant it, and how to rotate their crops to reduce harvest losses from drought and extreme heat. It turns NASA Earth observation data (NASA POWER climate records, MODIS vegetation, SRTM terrain) into plain-language answers: how the farm's area is doing today, which crops fit the local climate and the water the farmer actually has, and which rotation protects the soil. We piloted it in Sonora, Mexico, where drought left most wheat fields unplanted in 2025, and it works anywhere on Earth by changing the location.
details:
What it does. The farmer sets the farm location on an interactive map (or uses GPS) and gets:

- Today in your area: soil moisture, rainfall this month, temperature, and nearby planted fields, each compared with the 30-year normal for this time of year.

- Climate of your area: which months are good or dangerous (frost, extreme heat, dry months).

- What can I plant? A one-line verdict for 7 crops (e.g., "Yes, if you have guaranteed irrigation"), the best sowing window, water needed, local risks, and a 6-month outlook.

- Your soil: texture, organic matter, pH, current moisture, and slope, explained without charts, each with a "what to do."

- Is there enough water? With the farmer's hectares and allocated irrigation, it shows which crops fit and which fall short.

- Your next 3 seasons: rotation plans (keep the same crop, rotate to protect the soil, save water), rated for water use, soil health, and drought risk.

- Ask the AI: a chat assistant (voice input and read-aloud) that answers using the app's own calculations and NASA data as tools. It never invents numbers, and it leaves the decision to the farmer.

How it works. A Python (FastAPI) backend queries the data sources, caches them, and applies transparent, adjustable agronomic rules. The frontend is HTML/CSS/JavaScript, designed for phones. The crop catalog (wheat, maize, safflower, chickpea, beans, sorghum, canola) combines local data from Mexico's agricultural research institute (INIFAP) with FAO references, and cites the source of every value. Outside the pilot region, sowing windows are estimated from local NASA POWER climate, so the tool scales globally.

Benefits. A better decision before spending a single peso: matching crops to the water actually available, rotating to keep soil fertile, and fewer unplanted fields, which supports food security.

Tools. Python, FastAPI, JavaScript, Leaflet, Claude API (Anthropic).

Live prototype: https://cropy-6u4b.onrender.com
dataRefs: NASA POWER – Daily & Climatology API (temperature, rainfall, root-zone soil moisture)
ORNL DAAC MODIS Web Service (MODIS NDVI access)
SRTM – Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (elevation & slope)
NASA GIBS – MODIS Terra True Color imagery (map layer)
projectRefs: ISRIC SoilGrids – soil texture, pH, organic carbon
Open Topo Data – SRTM elevation API
INIFAP – Agenda Técnica Agrícola de Sonora 2026
FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 24 – Crop water requirements
FAO ECOCROP – crop temperature and pH requirements
Cropy crop catalog (sources cited per value)
OpenStreetMap – map tiles and place names
Anthropic Claude API – in-app AI assistant
